claims.text: Pulumi's component state migrations let component authors ship an upgrade path with the component; a migration translates the saved state of a component and its children before Pulumi works out which resources need to change.
Component state migrations are a new Pulumi feature.
The Pulumi component state migrations API is experimental and may change.
A component state migrations discussion exists at github.com/pulumi/pulumi/discussions/24799.
The v1 example uses the legacy `awsx.classic.ec2.Vpc` component and creates a VPC with one isolated subnet, a route table and association, and an internet gateway.
Replacing an AWS VPC requires replacing a security group that refers to the VPC's ID (per AWS CloudFormation EC2 SecurityGroup VpcId docs).
A replacement database does not automatically contain the old database's data; and the example does not create a database.
The v2 example uses the modern `awsx.ec2.Vpc` component.
The v3 example removes AWSX and declares resources directly with `@pulumi/aws`.
Across all three versions of the example, the AWS resource IDs stay the same and the security group continues to use the same VPC.
The resource trees for v1, v2 and v3 of the example show the resource types and names Pulumi tracks (e.g., v1 awsx:x:ec2:Vpc, v2 awsx:ec2:Vpc, v3 aws:ec2/vpc:Vpc).
Pulumi state records each resource and component with a URN, and managed resources also have a provider ID.
Legacy AWSX wraps the subnet and internet gateway in separate components; modern AWSX removes those wrappers; the subnet's Pulumi name changes from vpc-isolated-0 to vpc-isolated-1.
Pulumi aliases handle changes to a resource's name, type, or parent when saved state remains compatible, but cannot remove component wrappers and transfer references.
Pulumi resource options accept a `stateMigrations` option taking a migration callback, alongside aliases.

The migration callback receives the aliased component's saved state followed by its children's state, and returns `newState` (complete set of replacement records) and `successors` (map from each disappearing old URN to its replacement URN).
The example's `rename` helper copies a saved record and changes URN, type, and parent, preserving the AWS resource ID and other saved fields.
The Pulumi engine uses successors mappings to update dependencies and resource references elsewhere in the stack.

Pulumi runs state migration callbacks in order, passing each result to the next; a legacy AWSX stack can upgrade directly to plain AWS; a modern AWSX stack skips the first migration; after both have run, callbacks return no result on later updates.
After a migration, Pulumi compares the new program with the migrated state and calls the provider for remaining changes; the example can still show in-place updates for provider defaults and tags.
Running `pulumi preview` evaluates the migration without saving it, and the update saves the migrated state.
When users upgrade a component with a registered migration, Pulumi runs the migration as part of normal preview and update without users writing the migration or editing stack state.
The pulumi/examples repo contains aws-ts-awsx-vpc-state-migration with all three programs and migration code.
A Pulumi docs guide exists at /docs/iac/guides/building-extending/components/state-migrations/ covering the callback contract.
State migration callbacks (the stateMigrations resource option) run during previews and updates when prior state exists.
State migration callbacks must be idempotent and return no result when the state no longer needs migration.
State migration callbacks rewrite state without performing provider operations.
A Pulumi component state migration is a pure function that transforms the saved state of a component and its children into the state expected by a new component version.
A Pulumi component state migration callback returns the updated state records and successor mappings.
In a Pulumi component state migration result, each successor mapping connects an old URN omitted from the result to the URN of the returned resource that takes its place.
If no migration is needed, a Pulumi component state migration callback returns no result.
Pulumi component state migration state entries use the checkpoint resource format, including fields such as urn, type, id, parent, provider, inputs, and outputs.
The option reference at /docs/iac/concepts/resources/options/statemigrations/#callback-api explains the callback API.
A Pulumi state migration callback that returns no result can remain attached when using update plans or targeted updates.
The restrictions on state-changing results of Pulumi state migrations, when using update plans or targeted updates, do not require removing an already-applied migration.
